reviewStatus: Draft written by the build, pending clinical review (Nabeeha). Not a validated clinical association table.
label: Possible spaceflight factors. A symptom MAY be related to these hazards. The app cannot establish the cause of a symptom for one person, and these links never change the status.

source.label: NASA Human Research Program: Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight

hazards.name: Space radiation
hazards.summary: Outside Earth's protective magnetic field, crew receive more radiation than on Earth.

hazards.name: Isolation and confinement
hazards.summary: Long periods in a small, isolated crew can affect sleep, mood, workload and concentration.

hazards.name: Distance from Earth
hazards.summary: Help from Earth is far away and communication can be delayed, so the crew must be more self-reliant.

hazards.name: Gravity (and the lack of it)
hazards.summary: Altered gravity shifts body fluids toward the head and affects balance, the heart and blood vessels, bones and muscles.

hazards.name: Closed or hostile environment
hazards.summary: The spacecraft is a closed system: cabin air (including CO₂), temperature, humidity, noise and lighting all shape how crew feel.

fatigue.why: Adapting to altered gravity is associated with tiredness in some crew.
Workload, schedule and confinement can affect sleep and energy.
Cabin conditions such as CO₂, temperature and lighting can affect alertness.
Radiation exposure is one factor worth reviewing when fatigue persists.

headache.why: Fluid shifting toward the head in altered gravity is associated with headache in some crew.
Raised cabin CO₂ is associated with headache in research on closed environments.

dizziness.why: Altered gravity affects the balance system and blood-pressure control.

nausea.why: Space motion sickness, linked to altered gravity, can include nausea.
Radiation exposure is one factor worth reviewing when nausea is unexplained.

difficulty_concentrating.why: Confinement, workload and sleep loss can affect concentration.
Raised cabin CO₂ is associated with reduced concentration in research on closed environments.

severe_breathing_difficulty.why: Cabin air is worth checking, but this symptom always gives RED: follow the approved protocol first.
